# M4 fixed fixtures

All expectations in this tree come from the legacy system, not from hand-written
values.  Two sources:

## Natural days

Ten directories (`2026-08-21` … `2026-11-12`) were exported read-only from
`Ubuntu-nnG8:/home/ubuntu/trading-radar` with:

```
ssh Ubuntu-nnG8 '/home/ubuntu/trading-radar/runtime/current-swing/bin/python - \
    --date <YYYY-MM-DD> --emit-json' < qp/collect/signals.py
```

Each directory holds the ten exporter files plus `manifest.json` (sha256/bytes) and
`fixture.json` (attempt history and branch metadata).  Nothing was written on the
legacy host.  2026-11-09/10/11 `trend_signals.json` was reconstructed from
`eod_target_decision.raw_signals_json`: the legacy database had migrated the same
data bar to 11-12, so the live tables no longer held point-in-time rows.  That is
recorded in each `fixture.json` `notes`.

Branch facts (verified against the legacy DB):

| day | latest run | signal path |
|---|---|---|
| 08-21 | `success/emitted` | weekly golden cross, `ok` → allowed |
| 08-27 | `partial/emitted` | daily volume breakout, `ok`; null `total_amount` |
| 09-24 | 2 attempts; latest `success/no_signal` | first attempt `failed/data_unavailable` |
| 10-23 | `partial/data_unavailable` | watchdog failure + daily notifications |
| 10-27 | 3 attempts; latest `success/no_signal` | watchdog “not finished” path |
| 11-03 | `success/no_signal` | 40/40 evaluated |
| 11-09/10/11 | `success/blocked` | `critical`, both signals blocked |
| 11-12 | `success/blocked` | real trend rows, digest not yet generated |

`test_m4_fixtures.py` replays every exported decision through qp's risk gate and
asserts the legacy `decision_state`/`risk_action`/`reason_code`.

## Synthetic branches

`tests/fixtures/m4/synthetic/legacy_expected.json` is generated by running the
legacy code itself on Ubuntu-nnG8:

```
ssh Ubuntu-nnG8 '/home/ubuntu/trading-radar/runtime/current-swing/bin/python -' \
    < tests/fixtures/m4/synthetic/generate_legacy.py \
    > tests/fixtures/m4/synthetic/legacy_expected.json
```

It pins the sha256 of the two legacy source files and covers:

- risk-gate matrix: `ok`, uppercase `OK`, `growth_blocked` (growth blocked,
  non-growth allowed), `critical`, `warning`, `unavailable`, unknown level,
  missing state, and state without `level` — all fail closed except `ok`;
- `daily_volume_breakout=true` on 80 deterministic bars, including the exact
  signal detail produced by `TrendConfirmStrategy`.

`test_m4_synthetic.py` replays the same inputs through `qp.signals.risk.gate_action`
and `qp.signals.eod.evaluate_target` and compares every field.

Inbound signature/duplicate/bad-`risk_check` and digest 0/20/>20 truncation live in
`test_m4_approved.py`; they exercise the same accepted/rejected/`queued_stub` and
`items[:20]` semantics read from `deploy/approved-signals/app.py` and
`scripts/export_execution_digest.py`.
